title: CurAItion Story Package
description: Output of the story-packager skill. Sits between the framing stage (user-needs-classifier) and the channel writers (substack-writer, linkedin-writer, tweet-thread, carousel-producer). It COMMITS to a single story (the selected candidate), CONSOLIDATES the story-candidate handoff + user-needs classification into one self-contained artifact so no downstream writer calls back upstream or re-derives, and SEPARATES a frozen cited-facts layer from a malleable craft layer. The fact/craft split mirrors the CurAItion MCP 'grounded facts vs interpretive lift' rule and is what makes the no-fabrication guarantee enforceable at render/publish time: a writer may rephrase `facts[]` and elaborate `editorial`, but may not introduce a claim absent from `facts[]`.

package_id.description: Stable id for this package, e.g. 'pkg-2026-07-02-<slug>'. Used by writers and publishers to correlate outputs back to the source story.

source.description: Provenance of the package itself — which upstream files and which single candidate it was built from. This is the COMMIT record: many candidates in, one story out.

story_candidate_file.description: Path/filename of the story-candidate-<date>.json this package committed to.

user_needs_file.description: Path/filename of the user-needs-<date>.json classification. Optional but strongly recommended — its absence means the tone/need block was inferred, not classified.

candidate_id.description: The single candidate id (from the source handoff's selected_candidate_id) this package was built from. The packager never carries an array of candidates.

mode.description: Carried from the scout. Sets the default register: 'cultural' -> evergreen/curious, 'click-bait' -> urgent/topical.

scope_verification.description: Carried through UNCHANGED from the scout handoff — the library-scope compliance receipt. Required-shape for cultural mode; may be omitted/curaition_used:false for a pure-web click-bait run.

virality.description: Carried from click-bait-scout when present. Omit on a cultural run.

facts.description: GROUND-TRUTH LAYER. Frozen, canonical, every item citation-backed. Consolidated from the candidate's the_signal_24h, the_depth_90d, why_now and any relationship_verifications. Writers may reorder, select by importance, and rephrase these, but may NOT assert anything not represented here. This array is what a publish-time QA gate diffs rendered claims against.

id.description: Stable fact id (f1, f2, ...). Referenced by editorial.narrative_spine[].supports.

claim.description: A single atomic, verifiable statement. One fact = one claim; do not bundle.

importance.description: 0-3. Lets short formats degrade gracefully: a tweet thread may keep only importance>=3; longform uses all.

layer.description: Which part of the source candidate this fact came from — preserves the CurAItion signal-vs-depth structure.

citations.description: At least one citation per fact — this is the fabrication guard. content_id present only for CurAItion-sourced items.

source.description: Origin tool, matching the scout provenance vocabulary.

confidence.description: Optional. Writers should hedge low-confidence facts, not state them flatly.

quotable_verbatim.description: True if the claim wording is safe to reproduce as-is (e.g. an exact figure or a checked quote).

editorial.description: CRAFT LAYER. Model-owned interpretation, seeded from the candidate (headline_hypothesis, why_it_matters, surprise_factor) and the classifier (angle_guidance, primary_need). Every substantive beat references facts by id so the through-line stays provably grounded. Headlines and hooks are generated HERE as a shared pool, so all channels share one voice rather than inventing four unrelated takes.

thesis.description: The one-sentence argument the whole story makes. The spine serves this.

headline_options.description: Channel-agnostic headline pool. Seeded from user-needs angle_guidance.headline_options and refined. Writers select + adapt; they do not originate.

dek.description: Standfirst / one-line summary. Doubles as the Substack subtitle candidate (note Substack truncates ~250 chars at a sentence boundary).

hooks.description: Pool of opening hooks, seeded from surprise_factor. tweet-thread and carousel lead with one of these.

pull_quotes.description: Quotable lines for pull-quotes / carousel slides / social cards. Must be consistent with facts[].

narrative_spine.description: THE reuse engine. One ordered set of beats; every channel maps it (longform -> sections, tweet-thread -> tweets, carousel -> slides). Because all channels share this spine, they provably tell the same story in the same order.

beat.description: Role of this beat. Common values: hook, context, tension, depth, why_now, so_what, cta. Not locked — a story may need its own beat.

point.description: The single idea this beat conveys, in plain language (not final copy).

beat_type.description: grounded = rests on cited facts (supports required, non-empty). lift = interpretive/analytical bridge with NO citation — the CurAItion 'lift' (e.g. a historical rhyme). Must be marked so a writer never mistakes it for a cited fact and never states it as flat fact. structural = mechanical beat with no claim (e.g. cta).

supports.description: fact ids this beat rests on. REQUIRED and non-empty when beat_type=grounded; MUST be empty/omitted when beat_type=lift or structural. Every id here MUST exist in facts[] (cross-check enforced by the skill, not by JSON Schema).

register.description: Default from source.mode; may be overridden.

primary_need.description: Carried from user-needs-classifier primary_need. All channels serve this need unless channel_plan overrides.

voice_notes.description: Free-text steering. Should defer to the my-writing-style profile for house voice rather than restate it.

assets.description: MEDIA MANIFEST. The single source of truth for every image, animation, video, and embeddable URL the story can use — the same manifest a Substack/publisher QA gate diffs the rendered output against. This is where SPEC-2026-004 asset metadata and Replicate-ephemerality flags originate. May be empty for a text-only story.

id.description: Stable asset id (e.g. 'hero', 'slide_3', 'clip1'). Referenced by channel_plan[].use_assets.

kind.description: 'embed' = an oEmbed-able external post (TikTok/IG/YouTube/X); everything else is a file we host.

origin.description: Where the asset came from. 'replicate' and any non-hosted origin are ephemeral risk.

uri.description: Current location. For origin=replicate this is typically a short-lived replicate.delivery URL — see durable/rehost_required.

durable.description: True only if uri is on a permanent host (Substack CDN, S3, a stable oEmbed source). Replicate/temp URLs are false.

rehost_required.description: True if the asset MUST be re-uploaded to the target platform's CDN before publish (the Replicate-URL-expiry guard). The publisher/QA layer acts on this flag.

embed_provider.description: For kind=embed only. Tells the writer to emit a bare URL for the platform to oEmbed. Providers NOT on a target platform's oEmbed list need a fallback (poster image + link).

fallback_asset_id.description: For content a target platform cannot embed (e.g. Replicate video on Substack, custom iframes): the id of a static poster/still asset to use instead. Enforces 'a fallback exists' rather than silent drop.

alt.description: Accessibility text. Required in practice for images; validated by the writer, not the schema.

prompt.description: For generated assets: the generation prompt, kept for reproducibility.

channels.description: Which channels this asset is intended for (e.g. ['substack','carousel']). A hint, not a hard limit.

channel_plan.description: LATE-DIVERGENCE steering. Declares WHAT each channel should lead with and how far to lean; it never contains rendered copy. Writers decide HOW. Keys are writer skill names; unknown keys are allowed so new writers can be added without a schema change.

register.description: Optional per-channel override of editorial.tone.register (e.g. LinkedIn 'professional').

need_emphasis.description: Optional per-channel override of the primary_need served.

use_assets.description: asset ids to use on this channel (must exist in assets[]).

beats.description: Ordered subset of narrative_spine beats to include on this channel.

format_readiness.description: Per-target-format sufficiency signal, so a writer acts on the substance ceiling instead of discovering it mid-draft. Keys are format/writer names (e.g. 'long-form-substack', 'ig-carousel'); unknown keys allowed so new writers need no schema change. The packager reports how much substance exists — it does not pad to hit a length.

reason.description: Why it's not ready (present when ready=false).

needs.description: What must be added to make it ready (e.g. 'generated hero', 'price chart').

enrichment.description: Concrete substance to fetch before drafting (e.g. 'more nations' kits', 'cited history for the heraldry beat').

provenance.description: Carried through end-to-end from the scout handoff, plus any enrichment the packager itself did. Every data_point traces to a tool.

source.description: Originating tool OR pipeline stage. Research tools (CurAItion/WebSearch/WebFetch) originate facts; 'user-needs-classifier' marks a value carried from the need-classification stage; 'story-packager' marks a value the packager itself derived/inferred (backfill). facts[].source deliberately allows ONLY the three research tools — a fact must trace to real evidence, never to a pipeline stage.

compliance.description: Assertible invariants a publisher/QA gate can check before anything goes live.

brand_safety.description: Carried from click-bait virality.brand_safety; default 'safe' for cultural. 'unsafe' must never be packaged.

promotional_flag.description: True if the source content was promo/sale intent — writers should not amplify it as editorial.

fabrication_guard.description: Human-readable statement of the invariant the packager asserts, e.g. 'every facts[].id has >=1 citation; every narrative_spine[].supports id exists in facts[]'.

backfill.description: Audit trail of every field the packager DERIVED rather than carried from upstream — populated whenever an input (especially the user-needs classification) was absent or incomplete. Makes gap-filling transparent and reversible: nothing is silently invented, and a reviewer can see exactly what was inferred and from what. Empty/omitted when the package was built from a complete story-candidate + user-needs pair.

field.description: Dotted path of the derived field, e.g. 'editorial.tone.primary_need'.

method.description: inferred = reasoned from candidate content; generated = net-new craft (hooks, headlines, spine); carried-transformed = reshaped from an upstream field; default = fell back to a schema/house default.

derived_from.description: Source fields or fact ids the value was derived from.
